source_review.notes: Checked current PostgreSQL 18 base-backup, manifest verification, WAL archive, and logical-dump documentation; MySQL 8.4 backup and mysqldump documentation; current SQLite online-backup and VACUUM INTO documentation; NIST contingency guidance; and Google SRE data-integrity guidance.

evidence: Defined backup identity/version/snapshot/history/log interval/manifest/key/provenance tuple, full/incremental/differential/synthetic artifacts, recovery chains, and capture completion.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Physical bytes, logical semantics, snapshot consistency, integrity, capture completion, and restore verification remain distinct.

evidence: Checked start/end intervals 1000..1400 and 2000..3200, identified the missing 2700..2900 WAL interval, verified three required objects, and confirmed the three-hour observed RPO example.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Endpoint inclusivity and segment rounding remain explicitly engine-specific.

evidence: Reviewed physical mixed-time cut plus complete log reconstruction, logical shared-snapshot coverage, atomic candidate publication, dependency-graph retention, and digest implication boundaries.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Recoverability conclusions retain identity, protocol, history, format, key, and tool premises.

evidence: Reviewed live file copying, multi-volume skew, independent logical snapshots, DDL drop/recreate, truncated upload, middle WAL gap, lost keys, deduplicated deletion, missing tablespaces, old/new formats, and compromised credentials.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Partial or unverified candidates never replace the previous complete generation.

evidence: Checked physical/logical cut coverage, complete manifest and log publication, history binding, key availability, isolated authority, and chain-safe retention; the executable fixture validated exact coverage and digests.
invariant_checking.notes: Checksums alone are not treated as snapshot, provenance, semantic, or restore proof.

evidence: Reviewed physical-cut, logical-cut, publication, chain-retention, and integrity-boundary arguments with all required assumptions stated.
proof_review.notes: The chapter stops at capture evidence and reserves restore proof for DBE-080.

evidence: Audited backup, complete, consistent, immutable, verified, recoverable, encrypted, isolated, RPO, RTO, current, and portable terminology.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Product protocols and portability claims are scoped to documented versions and formats.

evidence: CPython 3.14.4 reproduced the finite SHA-256 manifest/coverage fixture on macOS 13.7.8 x86_64.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The fixture does not perform a database snapshot, encryption, upload, or restore.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed protected-unit definition, physical and logical protocols, snapshots, DDL identity, manifests, publication, increments, keys, isolation, retention, method choice, evidence, and capture faults.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed tablespaces, multi-volume cuts, WAL gaps, object stores, multipart integrity, credentials, key escrow, ransomware isolation, legal holds, deduplication, monitoring, canarying, and tool-format rollback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter derives both backup representations from consistency and recovery obligations, supplies a passing manifest fixture, ten examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external database-vendor, storage-provider, security, legal, compliance, operations, or production review is claimed. Conclusions remain conditional on capture protocol, snapshot scope, object inventory, history/log continuity, formats, manifests, cryptography and keys, credentials, storage durability, retention graph, workload, tools, and future version drift.
